title: Character Classes, Quantifiers, and Anchors
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of character classes, quantifiers, and anchors in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply character classes, quantifiers, and anchors in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to greedy and lazy matching and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Character Classes, Quantifiers, and Anchors through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding character classes, quantifiers, and anchors helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Character Classes, Quantifiers, and Anchors helps you reason about character sets and ranges. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Character sets and ranges. Then connect it to Repetition. The remaining syllabus points—Start/end anchors, Greedy and lazy matching—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
